question: Refer to the exhibit. A host with a source address 10.10.10.10 sends traffic to multicast group 239.1.1.1. How do the vPC switches forward the multicast traffic?
context:
Topology: Source 10.10.10.10 -> Rendezvous Point -> Switch1 (Po10, Po1 vPC peer-link) <-> Switch2 (Po11, Po1), both connect via vPC 20 to a downstream switch -> Vlan100 -> Receiver.

Switch1# sh ip mroute
(*, 239.1.1.1/32), uptime: 02:10:23, igmp ip pim
  Incoming interface: port-channel10, RPF nbr: 10.0.1.1
  Outgoing interface list: (count: 1) Vlan100, uptime: 02:10:23, igmp
(10.10.10.10/32, 239.1.1.1/32), uptime: 00:44:09, ip pim mrib
  Incoming interface: port-channel10, RPF nbr: 10.0.1.1
  Outgoing interface list: (count: 1) Vlan100, uptime: 00:44:09, mrib

Switch2# sh ip mroute
(*, 239.1.1.1/32), uptime: 02:18:34, igmp ip pim
  Incoming interface: port-channel11, RPF nbr: 10.0.2.1
  Outgoing interface list: (count: 1) Vlan100, uptime: 02:18:23, igmp
(10.10.10.10/32, 239.1.1.1/32), uptime: 00:44:49, ip pim mrib
  Incoming interface: port-channel11, RPF nbr: 10.0.2.1
  Outgoing interface list: (count: 0)
imageNote: Diagram: Source 10.10.10.10 sends multicast through a Rendezvous Point router to Switch1 (Po10, Po1 vPC peer-link) and Switch2 (Po11, Po1); both connect via vPC 20 to a downstream switch feeding Vlan100 and the Receiver.
options: If multicast traffic is received on Switch1 over the vPC peer-link, the traffic is dropped
If multicast traffic is received on Po10 Switch1, the traffic is forwarded out on Po1 and Po20
If multicast traffic is received on Po11 Switch2, the traffic is forwarded out only on Po20
If multicast traffic is received on Po11 Switch2, the traffic is dropped.
